newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France announces preliminary merger terms.
newsitem.headline: Air France announces preliminary merger terms.

text.p: The merger between Air France and Air France Europe will be done on a basis of 29 to 32 Air France shares for one Air France Europe share, the state-owned national carrier announced on Friday.
The airline said the terms were preliminary and based on studies by merchant bank Lazard Frere for Air France and French bank Societe Generale for Air France Europe.
The merger is aimed at consolidating the group's position in both the domestic and international markets as European routes open up to cross-border competition.

The parity between Air France and Group Air France will follow on from the finalised parity decided for Air France and Air France Europe as the group's assets consist almost entirely of shares in the two airlines.
The exchange parities will be finalised during board meetings at the end of July.
After cancelling Air France's self-ownership following the merger with Groupe Air France SA, the French state will continue to hold a direct controlling interest of about 94.5 percent.
The ordinary and extraordinary general meetings of the three companies will make a decision on the merger project by mid September 1997.
The plans for the merger between long-distance carrier Air France and its European arm Air France Europe has sparked strikes by staff unhappy over changes in working terms and wages.
